edges.description: Arterial fibrosis, cellular hyperplasia, and medial remodeling directly produce focal or multifocal string-of-beads arterial stenosis.
FMD arteriopathy is associated with clinical hypertension.
Abnormal arterial wall architecture in FMD is associated with arterial aneurysms.
Abnormal arterial wall architecture in FMD is associated with arterial tortuosity.
FMD arteriopathy frequently presents with arterial dissection in affected arterial beds.
FMD arteriopathy frequently presents clinically with headache.
FMD arteriopathy frequently manifests with pulsatile tinnitus.
FMD arteriopathy is associated with transient ischemic attack as a major vascular event.
FMD arteriopathy is associated with stroke in clinical and registry cohorts.
FMD arteriopathy is associated with intracerebral aneurysms detected on angiographic surveillance.

Fibromuscular dysplasia is associated with myocardial infarction, and diagnosis may follow spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD), although few patients with FMD develop coronary artery dissection while multifocal FMD lesions are reported in 30-80% of patients with SCAD.
Polygenic dysregulation of actin cytoskeleton and intracellular calcium homeostasis in vascular smooth muscle cells alters vessel wall mechanics and drives systemic non-atherosclerotic arteriopathy.
